stimulus.source_note: Table: National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS) High School Athletics Participation Survey, as reported by the NFHS. Figures verified against NFHS reporting: 294,015 girls in 1971-72; more than 2 million girls by 1977-78; total participation about 3.9 million in 1971-72 and about 6.4 million in 1977-78. Title IX date verified: signed June 23, 1972.
stimulus.text:
Girls playing high school sports, National Federation of State High School Associations survey.

School year | Girls playing high school sports
1971-72 | 294,015
1977-78 | More than 2,000,000

All high school athletes, boys and girls together: about 3.9 million in 1971-72; about 6.4 million in 1977-78.

Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 banned sex discrimination in any education program receiving federal money.

stem: According to the table, what happened to girls' participation in high school sports between 1971-72 and 1977-78?

options.misconception: The table shows girls' participation rising from 294,015 to more than 2,000,000, not falling.

options.text: It rose from about 294,000 to more than 2,000,000

options.misconception: The table shows a rise from 294,015 to more than 2,000,000, not a flat line.

options.text: It passed boys' participation for the first time
options.misconception: The table gives girls' numbers and a total for all athletes, but it does not give boys' numbers for 1977-78.

rationales.A: The table shows girls' participation rising from 294,015 to more than 2,000,000.
rationales.B: The table gives 294,015 girls in 1971-72 and more than 2,000,000 girls in 1977-78.
rationales.C: The table shows a large rise, not a flat line.
rationales.D: The table does not give boys' numbers for 1977-78, so it cannot show girls passing boys.
rationales.general:
1. The table gives 294,015 girls playing high school sports in 1971-72.
2. By 1977-78, the number was more than 2,000,000.
3. That is a rise of more than six times in six school years.
4. Total participation also rose, from about 3.9 million to about 6.4 million athletes.
Remember: Read a table by comparing the same row across years before you draw a conclusion.
